items.body: Carlos Vergara, singer and bassist of Barcelona post-punk trio Low Blows, made the video himself this time. “SOS” comes out as a single with that video on 15 September 2026. The song is not new to the band’s catalogue: it is the second track of the self-titled album “Low Blows”, released on 9 January 2026, and now gets its own single release. The band describe the video as “a dreamlike and hypnotic piece reflecting the feelings of life, loss and companionship that run through the song.” Low Blows by Low Blows “SOS” sits between the opener “Vacío” and “Fix Me” on the ten-track album, which runs on to “Misleading Blind (Album Mix)”, “Cracks”, “Intermezzo”, “I Hate (Album Mix)”, “Overrated”, “Go! (Album Mix)” and “Fin”. Low Blows recorded the album throughout 2024 and 2025 in their homes, their practice room and at Estudi Nautilus, where Jordi Solans handled the recording. Matteo Vallicelli, drummer of The Soft Moon, produced it, Lluis Cots mixed it at Estudi Nautilus and Maurizio Baggio mastered it at La Distilleria. Irina Stanciulescu did the artwork and design and Eduardo Cañas took the band photographs. ‘SOS’ follows ‘Vacío’ and a remix release The single is the second the band pull from the album. Side-Line covered the first in January: Low Blows release ‘Vacío’, first single and video from self-titled 2026 album, with a video directed by Marta Szewczyk. Between the two singles, on 29 May 2026, Low Blows put out “Remixes”, a four-track set with “SOS – doomzdei Remix”, “Misleading Blind – Matteo Vallicelli Remix”, “Vacío – SARCOMA Remix” and “Go! – LADIVINA Remix”. The new video for “SOS” is in-house work: Vergara made it himself, and the band signed the announcement as “Carlos & Low Blows”. About Low Blows Low Blows began in the mid-2010s as the solo project of Chilean musician Carlos Vergara, then living in Ibiza after his earlier bands Federación de Boxeo and This Co. The first two EPs, “Holes To Fill” (2016) and “Flesh” (2017), came out on the Manchester label Sister 9 Recordings and built on programmed electronics and guitars; a self-released digital EP, “Beyond The Flesh”, followed in 2018. The move to Barcelona turned the project into a band, with Rubén Carballo on drums, Andrés Silgado of Venus Fly Trap on guitar and, for a time, Marcel Molina on keyboards, alongside Vergara on bass and vocals. A run of singles from 2019 onwards, among them “Stranger”, “Low Blows” and “Skin”, led to the debut album “Cruel”, released in April 2020 on the Barcelona label Siete Señoritas Gritando. The standalone track “Ficción” appeared in 2021, followed by “Hate”, “Misleading Blind” and “I Hate” in 2023, and the singles “Normal” and “Go!” in 2024. The band’s own line for the sound is “post-punk for a hype, hyper, post and lost era”, and the songs mix post-punk, darkwave, industrial and new wave elements with lyrics in both Spanish and English. The self-titled second album, released on 9 January 2026 and produced by Matteo Vallicelli, gathered album mixes of “I Hate”, “Misleading Blind” and “Go!” with new material such as “Vacío”, “SOS” and “Cracks”. Low Blows now work as a trio of Vergara, Carballo and Silgado, and “SOS”, out as a single with its video on 15 September 2026, is the second track they lift from that record.
items._cn_summary: 巴塞罗那后朋克三人组Low Blows为其专辑同名曲《SOS》推出单曲及自制视频，该曲原为2026年1月发行的十轨专辑第二首。乐队称视频呈现梦幻而催眠的氛围，呼应歌曲中关于生命、失去与陪伴的主题。专辑录制于2024至2025年间，由The Soft Moon鼓手Matteo Vallicelli制作，在家庭、排练室及Estudi Nautilus完成，后期由Maurizio Baggio于La Distilleria母带处理。此前乐队已发行首支单曲《Vacío》及一张四曲混音合辑。主唱Carlos Vergara为智利音乐人，项目始于2010年代中期，后从个人计划发展为完整乐队，延续早期EP中的电子与吉他基底，并融入更丰富的暗潮质感。

items.body: After two self-released albums, Bagger 258 have a label. “Der Technokrat”, a two-track digital single, came out on August 28, 2026 through Scanner, the Dark Dimensions imprint that also handles The Saint Paul, Resistor and Akalotz. The Augsburg EBM duo of Nico von der Eisenmühle and Tim Schmelzer pair the original (3:31) with “Der Technokrat (The Saint Paul Edit)” (3:45), reworked by label-mate The Saint Paul. The single is available to stream and download on Bandcamp, where it sits in the Scanner catalogue alongside the label’s other 2026 releases, and on the usual streaming services. There is no physical edition. Der Technokrat by Bagger 258 What ‘Der Technokrat’ is about The band describe the song as a story in two halves: an authority that demands obedience, then a workforce that stops obeying. In the label notes they write that the track “explores the conflict between totalitarian control and individual resistance within an industrialized system” and that “the initial oppression gives way to open revolt: the working class refuses to comply, dismantles the existing power structures, and confronts the corrupt leadership with a collective claim to self-determination.” The theme continues the factory-floor vocabulary that runs through the Bagger 258 catalogue, from the albums “Ode an die Arbeit” and “Aufwärts gehts bergab”, where track titles include “Arbeiterwut”, “Werkshalle 4” and “Schicht im Schacht”. Musically the duo stay with the stripped-down, bassline-led EBM they have used since their debut. The label notes describe the track as built on “a relentless, machine-driven foundation of pounding beats, forceful basslines, and a dark, high-energy atmosphere”. “Der Technokrat” is the first new Bagger 258 material since the second album “Aufwärts gehts bergab”, released on February 20, 2026, and the first Bagger 258 release to appear on Scanner. The duo had already remixed for the label: their version of “The Undertaker” by Gamma Vortex came out through Scanner in September 2025. About Bagger 258 Bagger 258 formed in Augsburg, Germany as the EBM duo of Nico von der Eisenmühle and Tim Schmelzer, both also members of Projekt 26. They set out to revive the direct, bass-driven style associated with Anhalt EBM. In a Side-Line interview Schmelzer said they “were on a mission to resurrect something no one seemed to be messing with anymore – that punchy, in-your-face Anhalt EBM”. Von der Eisenmühle summed up the Bagger 258 method in the same conversation: “we’re after basslines that make you stomp, a brutal vibe, and tunes that stick with you.” The self-released debut album “Ode an die Arbeit” came out on November 24, 2023, mixed by Daniel Hallhuber of Young & Cold Records in Augsburg and mastered by Stefan Poiss of Mind.In.A.Box, and reached first place in the Deutsche Alternative Charts. Side-Line reviewed it in February 2024 and interviewed the duo the following month. Two digital singles followed in 2024: “Körperkommando” on June 21, with remixes by Kreign, Tension Control and Gamma Vortex, and “Alter Mann” on November 19. Both title tracks were carried over to the second album. “Aufwärts gehts bergab” arrived on February 20, 2026 as a digital release and a CD digipak limited to 258 copies, mixed and mastered by Krischan Jan-Eric Wesenberg at Studio 600 in Gelsenkirchen, Its thirteen tracks run “Arbeiterwut”, “Alter Mann”, “Funktion, Kontrolle!”, “Werkshalle 4”, “Erzengel”, “Körperkommando”, “Exakt!”, “Body 258”, “…und der Rest ist Geschichte” and “Schicht im Schacht”, closed by remixes of “Werkshalle 4” by Nachtmahr, of “…und der Rest ist Geschichte” by NordarR and of “Body 258” by Menticide. The duo play Nocturnal Culture Night 19 in Deutzen on the weekend of September 4-6, 2026. Both albums and the 2024 singles remain available through the band’s own Bandcamp page, separate from the Scanner catalogue that hosts the new single. “Der Technokrat” moves the project from self-release to the Scanner / Dark Dimensions roster.
items._cn_summary: Bagger 258 在签约 Scanner 厂牌后推出双曲目数字单曲《Der Technokrat》，延续其标志性的精简 EBM 路线。原曲以沉重的鼓机、压迫感强烈的贝斯线和黑暗高能量氛围构建出工业化的听觉场景，主题围绕威权统治与劳工反抗展开，呼应乐队一贯的工厂叙事。同厂牌音乐人 The Saint Paul 的混音版本在原作基础上加入个人处理，为同一素材提供不同的节奏层次。整体作品在风格上忠于 Anhalt EBM 传统，强调直接、冲击力强的身体律动，但在声音设计上未见明显突破，属于该类型框架下的扎实呈现。对于偏好工业舞曲的听众而言，这首单曲提供了同类语境中行之有效的听觉体验。

items.body: Three new tracks in thirteen minutes: that is the whole of “Melting Point X1”, the digital EP that Chainreactor released on August 28, 2026 through ProNoize, the Dark Dimensions imprint that has carried the project since 2009. The Düsseldorf industrial techno project of Jens Minor pairs the EP with an official video for the opening track, “Permagna”, which went up on the label’s YouTube channel the same day. The EP consists of “Permagna” (4:52), “Maybe, Maybe not” (4:30) and “S!ck Mode” (3:35). It is a digital-only release, available to stream and download on Bandcamp, where it is also part of the ProNoize label discography. Melting Point X1 by Chainreactor ‘Permagna’ and the sound of ‘Melting Point X1’ ProNoize presents the EP as a return to the project’s first records. The label text calls the three cuts “raw, hard-hitting, and unapologetically dirty” and says the EP “embraces the project’s original DNA: no gimmicks, no compromises”. Chainreactor has built its tracks on samples rather than sung vocals since “Interlinked” in 2020, after a period with Kay Schäfer as singer, and the label text places the new EP in that line. Side-Line has reviewed each of the last five Chainreactor albums and EPs, from “Interlinked” in 2020 to “War Machinery” in 2025. “Melting Point X1” is the second Chainreactor release of 2026 after the one-track digital single “Unintentional Presence – Part 2” on April 24, and the first EP since “The Essence” in 2021. It also continues a direction Side-Line noted on the last album: the “War Machinery” review described Minor as circling “back to his roots – delivering raw power through a perfect fusion of Dark-Electro, Industrial, and Rave”, with spoken-word samples in place of vocals. That twelve-track album, which includes “No Apologies”, “Roar”, “Go”, “Kalt” and “Unendlichkeit”, was the tenth in the Chainreactor catalogue. ProNoize is the harder electronic arm of Dark Dimensions, the German label group that also runs Scanner, and it has released every Chainreactor album since the 2009 debut. Its Bandcamp catalogue now lists 86 releases, and the new EP is sold there as a single digital download rather than as part of a physical edition. About Chainreactor Chainreactor started in 2009 as the solo project of German producer Jens Minor. The debut album “X-Tinction” came out on ProNoize the same year, followed by “Insomniac” (2011), “The Silence & The Noise” (2013), “Mass Driver” (2014), “Dirt” (2015) and “Decayed Values” (2017), all on the same label. Kay Schäfer joined as a second member and singer during that stretch, and a “Rare Stuff & Remixes” compilation collected loose tracks in 2017. Minor mixes hard techno, power noise, EBM and trance elements into a club-oriented industrial sound that he has called “a testing range where I can put all the influences of music that I like to something new” in a Side-Line interview. The seventh album, “Interlinked” (2020), dropped vocals again in favour of samples, a decision Schäfer, who had become a full member and the singer on the preceding albums, explained in that interview: “Chainreactor is about creating a certain atmosphere and feeling and this is done through the music itself and not through lyrics.” Videos for “Interlinked”, “Grey” and “The Wicked” accompanied that twelve-track album. The EP “The Essence” followed in 2021, then the albums “Techno Body Device” (2022), “Venom” (2023) and, as a solo project once more, “War Machinery” (2025), the tenth Chainreactor album. The digital singles “Welcome To The Deep” (four tracks) and “Destroyer Of Worlds” (two tracks) followed in 2024, then “Roar” and “30 Ghosts 2K25” in 2025, all of them on ProNoize. “Melting Point X1” follows “War Machinery” by a year and returns to the format of the project’s early, sample-driven records.
items._cn_summary: Chainreactor在2026年8月通过ProNoize发行数字EP《Melting Point X1》，包含三首共约十三分钟的曲目，并配有一支官方视频。这是该工业电子项目回归早期声音的作品，厂牌文案强调其原始、粗粝、不加修饰的特质。自2020年专辑《Interlinked》之后，项目放弃了人声演唱，转为使用口语采样和重型节拍构建声响。本EP延续了2025年《War Machinery》以来的方向，将暗电、工业与锐舞元素融合，呈现出直接而具有冲击力的听觉体验。作为Jens Minor的个人计划，Chainreactor自2009年起持续在ProNoize发行作品，此次数字EP也是其2026年的第二张发行，继续巩固了他在这一领域的标志性路线。

items.body: The age-old adage: what do you get when Genesis's Steve Hackett and Marillion's Steve Rothery cross proggy paths? Hopefully you haven't been asking that question too long, since The Roaring Waves is the first instance of the duo collaborating studio-wise. Yes, Rothery joined Hackett during the latter's 2013 concert at the Hammersmith Odeon, but this marks the premiere point of studio cooperation. It's quite surprising that these two musicians, each with decades upon decades of expertise in adjacent fields, only released a project last Friday. Hackett's been silent since 2023's The Circus and the Nightwhale, and Rothery's last release, The Ghosts of Pripyat, is nine years Nightwhale's elder. Eight years in the making led up to this (which explains the dip in activity from the respective players), so it's about time some classic, guitar-driven prog came my way, and I'd never ignore an artistic couplet such as Hackett & Rothery, so follow me as we dive straight into The Roaring Waves. It comes as no surprise, considering the kith and kin that are two progressive rock guitarists, that the record is purely instrumental. Think of it comfortably, rather than a full-throttle, blistering shredfest akin to some breakaway Dream Theater endeavor. The Steves rely on textural atmospherics instead of masturbatory showiness to craft the record's concept: the "profundity of the sea". Don't bend your legs and widen your feet just yet–the two artists bring the ocean to you. Whether they do so through a steady rocking pattern or electronic-laden passages is up to the natural course of Mother Nature's vast waterscapes. While the idea is intriguing, Hackett and Rothery only periodically conjure the nautical imagery exhibited on the album's cover. While the masterful duo trade winding, melancholic notes over shifting drum patterns (see "Sandsend," "The Black Sea") or simple ambience ("K-129"), there aren't enough sonic tinges to communicate such an expansive, oceanic environment. Little nods, like the natural sound effects in the opening track "The Storm," or the electronic pitter-patter sprinkled throughout The Roaring Waves' bulk of songs, rein me in from deeming the LP a standard instrumental release.This brings up a talking point heavily debated within the rock and metal community. Are instrumental records boring? Intrinsically, they are, when considering the heaviness of the genre. Of course, ambient albums surely mustn't include lyrics, but should progressive rock? Plenty of classics, like Camel's The Snow Goose or Mike Oldfield's myriad of sprawling epics, benefit from the instrumental's activity. There's nothing stagnant about these examples, hence their cult fame. The Roaring Waves waits until the final song, "Pacific Coast Highway," to supply any rocking action, and even that doesn't honestly fit in with the sea-ness. The twangy rip from Hackett's harmonica and symphonic feel aren't choices I would've made to muster oceanic vibes, and for this excitement, I had to tread thirty-eight-or-so minutes of consoling yet unwavering waters. I didn't plunge to the depths of The Roaring Waves expecting a tsunami; more of a point break. Instead, my bark swayed gently, rendering the gumption I gathered unnecessary.They can play their water pans and layer keyboard upon synth, but I want more from these illustrious talents. Granted, I wasn't a huge fan of Marillion (or neo-prog, actually), and Genesis fell off for me, along with everyone else, when the 80s pop wave decimated prog. Hackett helped the band navigate some of the finest recordings of the 70s; however, he should've administered a larger dose of his vintage spirit with his guitarmate. Dexterously, this collaboration fell short, but if you need forty-five minutes of simple backing tunes, you'll find these waves better fit for your boat. The Roaring Waves (24-bit HD audio) by Steve Hackett, Steve Rothery

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Grimalkin by Pattern-Seeking Animals is a great push forward for the band into their symphonic prog roots, but still keeping their well known penchant for pop hooks. Composed entirely by keyboardist John Boegehold, it showcases his great songwriting abilities that enabled him to start writing for Spock's Beard, after the departure of Neal Morse. Overall the band's performances are excellent, with great vocals and some impressive melodic guitar playing from Ted Leonard. While it may not be their most gripping release, it is a great progression for their sound, overtaking The Flower Kings as the current kings of symphonic prog. I'd give this a mid to high 7 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is I Dream The World.

items.body: Review by Abrasmatheus — This was my first time listening to No Earthly Connection, and I came to it with high expectations. I have always been a big fan of Yes, so I already knew how impressive Rick Wakeman could be with keyboards. Even so, this album was a very pleasant surprise.From the beginning, I was impressed by the beautiful melodies and the strongly progressive character of the music. I would describe it mainly as Symphonic Prog, Progressive Rock and, of course, with strong Classical influences. The arrangements are complex, grandiose, melodic and atmospheric, but the music never loses its emotional side.Rick Wakeman is obviously the great highlight here. This album is a wonderful showcase of his talent with keyboards and synthesizers. Many of the things I love about his playing in Yes are present here as well, but in a more personal setting where he can really show what he is capable of. His synthesizers give the album an enormous sense of grandeur.I also really enjoyed the way the album works as a complete experience. I always appreciate progressive rock albums that encourage you to sit down and listen to the whole record instead of simply picking individual songs. No Earthly Connection works particularly well in this format.The concept is another aspect that made the album special to me. The first five sections form Music Reincarnate: The Warning, The Maker, The Spaceman, The Realisation and The Reaper. The concept deals with the idea of a "musical soul" accompanying a human being through life and continuing through reincarnation after death. Wakeman presented it as a possibility rather than as an absolute explanation, exploring ideas about life, death, evolution and things that are difficult to explain. I found this particularly fascinating because of the spiritual dimension of the album. The recurring idea of the music of the soul, together with references to reincarnation and the journey of the soul, gives the music an additional meaning for me. The atmosphere is cosmic, epic, dramatic and almost cinematic, but also very beautiful and emotional.My favorite part is The Warning, especially its final section. There is a vocal passage that reminds me a lot of Jon Anderson, and when it becomes more dramatic, I absolutely love it. It is one of those moments that immediately caught my attention.The Maker has an incredible Rick Wakeman synthesizer passage that sounds unmistakably like him. It gives the album an enormous sense of grandeur and is one of the moments that most reminded me why I enjoy his work with Yes.I also really like The Spaceman, especially because of its beautiful melody and the way it continues the idea of the musical soul. The Realisation is another favorite. I love its melody and lyrics, and I found it particularly interesting how the album continues returning to the idea of the soul and its journey.The Reaper is also excellent. It has another wonderful melody and recalls ideas from earlier parts of the album, which gave me the impression of a return or continuation of the soul. This is my own interpretation, but I really enjoyed experiencing the album this way. The instrumental ending is also fantastic and reminded me of some moments from Yes.Finally, The Prisoner has a more dramatic character and fits very well into the overall atmosphere. The final piece, The Lost Cycle, also helps give the album a sense of completion, extending its ideas into questions about evolution and possible advanced civilizations beyond Earth. (Wikipedia)Honestly, I did not find any uninteresting moments here. For me, the album is beautiful from beginning to end.The vocals are also extremely important. They contribute greatly to the atmosphere and emotional impact of the album. Without them, I don't think No Earthly Connection would have the same character.The production is very good as well. Wakeman produced the album and played an impressive variety of keyboard instruments, including Moog synthesizers, Mellotron, Hammond C3 organ, pipe organ, grand piano, electric piano, clavinet and harpsichord. The instrumentation is very rich, but the keyboards and synthesizers remain the main identity of the record. (rwcc.com)At several points, the album reminds me of Yes, particularly because of Wakeman's keyboard style and the use of synthesizers. I can also hear similarities with other progressive rock bands from the 1970s.I wouldn't say that the album is radically original compared with everything else being produced in progressive rock at the time. I don't hear something that completely separates it from the progressive rock of its era. However, this does not take anything away from its beauty or magnitude.For me, the three greatest strengths are the vocals, the synthesizers and the melodies.I honestly cannot point to any significant weaknesses. The album works very well as a complete experience.Since this is the first Rick Wakeman solo album I have listened to, I cannot yet compare it with the rest of his solo discography. But this album certainly made me interested in exploring more of his solo work.I will definitely listen to No Earthly Connection many more times. It is an album that I enjoyed not only for its progressive rock qualities, but also because its ideas about the soul, reincarnation and existence gave the music a deeper personal meaning for me.Rating: 4/5No Earthly Connection is an album of beautiful melodies, impressive synthesizers, powerful vocals and grand progressive arrangements. Above all, for me, it is an album of music that feeds the soul.

items.body: The eight-track record features vocals from Alison Skidmore and Elaine Howley Andy Stott has shared details of his first album in five years, titled Late Loop. Spanning eight tracks, it features contributions from vocalists Alison Skidmore and Elaine Howley. Stott gave himself a number of parameters when he set out working on the record, deciding to use no basslines, no reverb and no effects, save for a delay unit. Stott previously worked with Skidmore on past material, including classic 2014 cut 'Faith In Strangers'. This album marks the first time he has collaborated with Howley, on the other hand. Watch a video for lead track 'Something In My Mind', featuring vocals from Howley, below. Modern Love will release Late Loop on 30 October... The post Andy Stott Unveils First Album in Five Years, ‘Late Loop’ appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Andy Stott时隔五年推出新作，通过设定严格创作限制——摒弃低音线、混响与各类效果，仅保留延迟效果器——构建极简而通透的声音空间。专辑共八首曲目，邀集两位歌手参与：曾合作过的Alison Skidmore与首次合作的Elaine Howley，后者在主打曲中献声。在如此克制的技术条件下，人声与延迟之间形成紧密互动，延续了Stott一贯的暗黑电子气质，同时呈现出不同于以往的去装饰化质感。这张专辑由Modern Love发行，值得关注其如何以减法策略重定义电子音乐的情绪张力。

items.body: The Prom on August 23, which was presented by the BBC Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Alain Altinoglu, concluded with a performance of Amérique by Edgard Varèses, having begun with Stravinsky’s Symphonies of Wind Instruments in its 1947 version, The Dvorak ‘Cello Concerto, with Gautier Capuçon soloist, and Debussy’s Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun. The title of the piece had dual meanings, just as Varèses’s intentions were multiple. The work was on one hand a sort of portrait of the active and bustling New York City, but it also had the intention of opening new, as it were, vistas of sound available for composition. The title implied both the new world as it existed, but also the possibility of exploration. So the music is full of energy and activity and the depiction of day to day noise in a specific way that was new in music. Although it has a momentary quite beginning (possibly referring to the beginning of The Afternoon of the Faun and offering a tribute to Debussy), Amérique’s energy and intensity is incessant and ever increasing. That intensity and energy was completely realized by this performance. The Prom on August 22 was presented by the Chineke! Orchestra, conducted by Jonathon Heyward and featured the soprano Angel Blue. It opened with a reconstruction of a work by the African American, British educated, at the Royal Academy of Music, composer, Edmund Thornton Jenkins. The work, which was conceived when he was a student in London, called Ballet, was reconstructed from existing parts and a piano reduction, by his great-newphew, Tuffus Zimbabwe. It was the first performance of any of Jenkins’s music on the Proms. The central work on the program was Samuel Barber’s Knoxville Summer of 1915, which featured Blue. The piece sets a text by James Agee and can be justifiably described as nostalgic. It is also arguably Barber’s best piece. The text is written in the first person, but Blue gave it a quality somewhat akin to what happens in Thorton Wilder plays, especially Our Town, where a character addresses the audience directly. She gave it an especially directly personal and expressive quality that was very moving and unforgettable. She followed the Barber with some songs from what is probably described these days as the American Song Book. Her performances of those pieces, including My Funny Valentine (Richard Rogers and Lorenz Hart), Our Love Is Here to Stay (Goerge and Ira Gershwin), That Old Black Magic (Harold Arlen and Johnny Mercer), and Puttin’ On the Ritz (Irving Berlin), was mostly masterful and compelling. For this listener the performance of My Funny Valentine compared favorably to Ella Fitzgerald’s recording. The order of the songs was not the same as what was listed in the program, and one of the songs listed was not performed. The concert concluded with a very lovely and lovely-sounding performance of the Dvorak Eighth Symphony. As is the current practice, the Prom on August 29, presented by the Oslo Philharmonic, conducted by Mirga Gražinytė-Tyla, was advertised as containing music by Stravinsky and Prokofiev without mentioning that it would be opened by the first Proms performance of Symphonic Poem no. 1, ‘Forest Morning’ by Øyvind Torvund. The work was as evocative as one might expect a piece with that title to be. It seemed to have at the beginning, random, or at least random seeming, recordings of birds, but those sound morphed into similar figures that were clearly played by instruments in the orchestra, so that after a while it wasn’t completely clear that there ever had been recordings of actual birds. The program quoted Torvund in saying “…I also like to think about all the smaller, perhaps psychedelic sounds in nature, those that are found naturally and can remind you of electronic sounds. The mirroring of sounds is one of the things that fascinates me the most.” So who knows? In any case, the shape and progress of the piece was compelling and impressive and very enjoyable. The Stravinsky work was the Violin Concerto, which was performed with the soloist Patricia Kopatchinskyaja. As her encore, regretting the absence of cadenzas and chances for soloistic displays in the piece, she played a very technically complicated and showy “candenza” which she had written based on material in the concerto. The concert concluded with a rousing performance of music from Romeo and Juliet by Prokofiev. As an encore at the end of the concert, the orchestra played another piece by Torvund, apparently orchestrated in the five previous days, entitled Starry Night. This one clearly made use of recorded sounds and was highly effective and also very enjoyable. The post BBC Proms Varese Barber Torvund Jenkins et al appeared first on Sequenza21.

items.body: Sixteen tracks, most of them under three minutes, make up the first Scaled Alps album. The Los Angeles band released “Let the Alpine Play” on 20 July 2026 as a digital album on their own Blue Hell imprint, available on Bandcamp and on streaming services. Scaled Alps mix heavy rock, electronics and post-punk atmosphere under the low baritone voice of James Quentin Devine. Let the Alpine Play by Scaled Alps Devine sings, Anthony Percoco plays keys and guitars, Sean McCarthy plays drums and Steve Fishman plays upright and electric basses. Stewart Tuttle recorded the album at The Altar Studios in North Hollywood. The songs started as a set of self-recorded demos called “The Desertion Sessions”, cut in two sessions that ran through day and night and produced more than thirty tracks; sixteen of them were then re-recorded in the studio’s Big Room with Tuttle. On their Bandcamp page the band describe the result as “celestial, infernal crime spree music”. Devine described the project and the way the record was made in an email to Side-Line: “JQD is a low-voiced singer moving between heavy rock, electronics, post-punk atmosphere and stranger pop; the voice remains the stable identity while the machinery changes. The record itself was made rapidly and largely without a click, leaving breath, strain, drift and imperfections audible.” He points to “Southerly” and “Celestial Sighs” as starting points. ‘Let the Alpine Play’ tracklist The album runs “Another Clock Song (The 7th Unveiling)”, “Celestial Sighs”, “Southerly”, “Space/Time”, “Muffler (Chrome Viscera)”, “T.T.M.S. (Sunyata)”, “You Got H-O-R-S, You Want E Too?”, “Pink Diamonds”, “Neo Noir (Stelvio)”, “Selling It”, “Slow Motion”, “Impro (The Imp of the Perverse/The Pimp of the Inverse)”, “I Think We Met in Setagaya (Maybe it Was Seville)”, “Lemon Zest”, “Tentacoli” and “Throwaway Lines (Leo II)”. Only “Slow Motion” and “Lemon Zest” pass the three-minute mark; “Selling It” lasts 38 seconds. The band also publish an 18-page “Owner’s Manual” with the lyrics and the album’s visual material, and the full package of production WAVs and MP3s is offered as a free public download from the Blue Hell site. About Scaled Alps Scaled Alps is the band of Los Angeles singer and lyricist James Quentin Devine, who also records under his own name and as JQD, and of instrumentalist Anthony Percoco. The Scaled Alps name first appeared as a featured credit on Devine’s solo track “Cynical Ploy”, released on 5 May 2022, ahead of his solo releases “James Quentin Devine Plays the Saxophone For You” and “3-PIT” later that year. “Let the Alpine Play”, recorded at The Altar Studios in North Hollywood with Stewart Tuttle, Sean McCarthy and Steve Fishman, is the first full album under the Scaled Alps name and the first release on the band’s own Blue Hell imprint.
items._cn_summary: Scaled Alps的首张专辑《Let the Alpine Play》收录十六首短曲，多数不足三分钟，在洛杉矶The Altar Studios的Big Room快速录制，刻意不使用节拍器，保留呼吸、紧张与瑕疵。乐队融合重摇滚、电子和后朋克氛围，以James Quentin Devine的低沉男中音为稳定标识，Anthony Percoco负责键盘与吉他，节奏部分由鼓手和双贝斯手构成。歌曲源自两场昼夜不断的“Desertion Sessions”三十余首样带，再精选重录，并随专辑发布十八页手册与免费工程文件下载。作品跨越多种情绪，曲名怪异，如38秒的“Selling It”，体现出即兴与反常规的结构。其价值在于快速录音保留的即兴感与独立发行方式。

items.body: HANDS will return to Berlin’s Urban Spree on Saturday, 2 January 2027 for another New Year edition of HANDS Label Night, bringing together six live projects and two DJ sets for an evening moving through rhythm’n’noise, industrial techno and the harder edges of electronic music. The live line-up features SONAR, NULLVEKTOR, GREYHOUND, ICD-10, ESPECTRA NEGRA and MARIE, while HANDS founder Udo Wiessmann and HELLS will take care of the DJ sets. The night begins at 19:00, with doors also opening at 19:00. It is a particularly representative cross-section of the label’s history and current direction. SONAR, the Belgian project of Dirk Ivens and Eric Van Wonterghem, remain one of the defining names associated with rhythm’n’noise; their most recent HANDS album, “Future Cries”, arrived in 2023 after a nine-year album break. NULLVEKTOR, Stefan Böhm’s long-running project, connects industrial techno with rhythm’n’noise and has been part of the HANDS orbit since the early 2000s. GREYHOUND return with their uncompromising rhythmic approach, while ICD-10 arrive after releasing “Quantum Disruption” in May 2026, an album built around industrial-techno propulsion, seismic low-end pressure and tightly controlled rhythmic structures; it also includes a collaboration with GREYHOUND on “Merging Power”. ESPECTRA NEGRA, the project of Verónica Mota, brings the darker and more abrasive end of industrial techno to the bill, while MARIE completes the six-act live programme. The event also continues what has become a recurring Urban Spree tradition. HANDS staged its previous New Year Label Night there on 3 January 2026, following other Berlin editions at the same venue. The Dortmund-based label itself was founded by Udo Wiessmann in 1990 and became closely associated with the development of rhythm’n’noise while maintaining a catalogue extending into industrial techno, IDM, breakcore, ambient, electronica and sound art. HANDS Label Night Berlin – Saturday, 2 January 2027, Urban Spree Live: SONAR NULLVEKTOR GREYHOUND ICD-10 ESPECTRA NEGRA MARIE DJ: UDO WIESSMANN HELLS Doors / Start: 19:00 Both e-tickets and limited physical hard tickets are available through HANDS Bandcamp. For those who prefer to begin the year with considerably more noise than champagne, Berlin already has its first serious industrial appointment of 2027. About HANDS Udo Wiessmann founded HANDS in 1990 in his home town of Fürth in Franconia as an outlet for his own projects Atrum, Severance and Winterkälte, starting with limited-edition cassettes and industrial compilations. The first CDs followed in 1994 and the first vinyl, a Winterkälte 7″, in 1995. In the late 1990s the label moved to Dortmund and began issuing full albums on CD, opening with the debuts of Orphx, Ah Cama-Sotz and Needle Sharing and continuing with Mono No Aware, S.I.N.A. and Xabec. Winterkälte’s drum’n’noise records became reference points for the rhythm’n’noise scene, and the catalogue later extended into industrial techno, IDM, drum & bass, breakcore, ambient, electronica and sound art with acts including Nullvektor, Empusae, Geistform, Wieloryb, Monolith, Greyhound and Ontal, alongside reissues of The Klinik back catalogue. Between 1997 and around 2004 the label also ran the vinyl-only power electronics and noise sublabel 220N, and most of its sleeves and paper CD packs are designed by Nicola Bork. Live events sit at the centre of the label’s calendar. Wiessmann started the Forms of Hands label festival in 2001 with Michael Pfefferkorn and the promoter LaborNeun; since 2012 it has taken place at the Förderturm in Bönen in the Ruhr area, and each edition comes with a “Forms Of Hands” compilation of exclusive tracks by the acts on the bill. The Beats and Noise event at the Kulttempel in Oberhausen returns on 10 October 2026 with Sonar, Ancient Methods, Maschinenkrieger KR52, Hysteresis, ICD-10 and Mortaja. In Berlin, a HANDS Label Night at Bi Nuu marked the label’s 28th year in January 2018 before the series settled at Urban Spree, where it now runs twice a year: a summer edition (8 July 2023, 28 June 2025 and 27 June 2026) and a New Year edition. The sold-out 4 January 2025 night had Sonar, Eric De Vries, Greyhound, Templer, Espectra Negra and Phasenmensch on the bill, and 3 January 2026 brought Ah Cama-Sotz, Maschinenkrieger KR52, Supersimmetria, 16Pad Noise Terrorist and Incendie. The 2 January 2027 night is the third New Year edition of HANDS Label Night at Urban Spree in a row.

items.body: Thirteen new extended versions, cut from the original tapes, make up the next Telex release. “MAXI” arrives on Mute on 4 December 2026 as a double album on transparent red and blue vinyl and as a CD, with a digital release to follow in 2027. The launch track is a maxi version of “Moskow Diskow”, the 1979 single from the Belgian synthpop trio’s debut album, now out as official audio on Mute’s YouTube channel. The album is available to pre-order. Telex were Marc Moulin (1942-2008), Dan Lacksman and Michel Moers, and the two surviving members went back to the original tapes to build the Maxi versions, which come with new mixes and new mastering. The album collects “Moskow Diskow”, “Soul Waves”, “L’Amour Toujours”, “Rock Around The Clock”, “Temporary Chicken”, “Dance To The Music”, “Eurovision”, “En Route Vers De Nouvelles Aventures”, “Rendez-Vous Dans L’Espace”, “Peanuts”, “Twist À Saint-Tropez”, “Spike Jones” and “We Are All Getting Old”, each carrying the “(Maxi)” suffix. The tracklist spells the opener “Moskow Diskow”, as on the original single, while the audio upload titles it “Moscow Diskow”. Telex revisit ‘Euro-vision’ and ‘Rock Around The Clock’ Two of the extended tracks come with a television history. “Euro-vision” was Belgium’s entry at the Eurovision Song Contest in 1980, where it finished 17th of 19 with 14 points. Moers described the entry as “very Situationist International, the worm in the apple.” The band set out to finish either first or last, and did neither. Their cover of Bill Haley’s “Rock Around The Clock”, slowed down and sung through a vocoder, brought the trio an invitation to perform on Top of the Pops in 1979; Mute calls it “a ticking, vocoderised, supremely deadpan robot parody of the original”. The later material on “MAXI” includes the cut-up “rap” of “Peanuts”, from 1988’s “Looney Tunes”, and “Rendez-Vous Dans L’Espace”. About Telex Telex formed in Brussels in 1978, when Marc Moulin, Dan Lacksman and Michel Moers set out to make electronic pop without guitars. Their first single was a cover of Les Chats Sauvages’ “Twist à Saint-Tropez”, and the debut album “Looking for Saint-Tropez” (1979) carried “Moskow Diskow” and “Rock Around The Clock”. “Neurovision” followed in 1980, the year of the Eurovision entry, and “Sex” in 1981, with lyrics co-written with Sparks. “Wonderful World” appeared in 1984 and “Looney Tunes” in 1988, after which the trio remixed its catalogue as “Les Rythmes Automatiques” in 1989 and then went quiet as a recording unit. The sixth and last studio album, “How Do You Dance?”, came out in 2006. Moulin died on 26 September 2008, and Telex announced their retirement that year. The partnership with Mute began in 2021 with “This Is Telex”, a 14-track compilation released on 30 April 2021 with the tracks newly mixed and remastered by Lacksman and Moers. It added two previously unreleased covers, “Dear Prudence” by The Beatles and “The Beat Goes On” by Sonny & Cher, both found while the compilation was being assembled. Mute then reissued the six studio albums, remastered from the original tapes, as a limited vinyl and CD “Telex” box set, announced in October 2022 with the teaser “EP1” and released on 14 April 2023. Three days later Lacksman and Moers sat down with Mute founder Daniel Miller for a public talk in Brussels (A night with Telex and Mute Records founder Daniel Miller in Brussels). Moers went on to release his second solo album, “As Is”, in 2024, led by the single “Microwaves” with Claudia Brücken of Propaganda. “MAXI” is the first Telex release of newly made versions since that box set, and the third stage of the Mute campaign after the compilation and the reissues.
items._cn_summary: Telex 的《MAXI》是一张将乐队经典曲目重新扩展混音的专辑，两位健在成员从原始母带出发，为十三首作品制作了新的加长版与母带处理。这些版本并非简单拉长，而是通过新混音赋予旧作更丰富的层次与空间感，保留了乐队标志性的冷漠机器嗓音与幽默解构姿态。开篇曲《Moskow Diskow》的加长版率先曝光，其复古未来主义质感与俱乐部节拍结合，既回溯了七十年代末的合成器流行源头，又以当代电子制作手法焕发新意。专辑中还包含《Euro-vision》与《Rock Around The Clock》等具有电视史背景的曲目，后者以 vocoder 慢速演绎，形成对原作的机械戏仿。整体上，这是一次对乐队自身历史的立体化重访，适合欣赏复古电子美学与实验性重混思维的听众。

items.album: Trauma Party release the video for ‘Roll Up (It’s The New Truth)’
items.excerpt: Martin Bowes of Attrition mastered it at The Cage in the UK, which is where the trail from a small New Zealand island reaches familiar ground. New Zealand post-punk band Trauma Party released the video for “Roll Up (It’s The New Truth)” on 1 September 2026 through their own YouTube channel. It is the fourth and last video single drawn from the debut EP “Because You’ve Been Good”, issued on 17 April 2026. The four-piece is based on Waiheke Island, off Auckland.
items.body: Martin Bowes of Attrition mastered it at The Cage in the UK, which is where the trail from a small New Zealand island reaches familiar ground. New Zealand post-punk band Trauma Party released the video for “Roll Up (It’s The New Truth)” on 1 September 2026 through their own YouTube channel. It is the fourth and last video single drawn from the debut EP “Because You’ve Been Good”, issued on 17 April 2026. The four-piece is based on Waiheke Island, off Auckland. Buddy Olson sings, Derek Solomon plays guitar and backing vocals, Ron K plays bass and Kirsty Swanney drums. The EP was recorded at the Dirt Track and at Vanguard Studios, mixed by Solomon at Vanguard, and mastered by Martin Bowes at The Cage. Bek Farr made the artwork. What Trauma Party say about ‘Roll Up (It’s The New Truth)’ The band place the song against political language that has stopped meaning what it says. “This song is not quiet; it screams at us all to wake up and beware ‘the new truth’ and the surreality of alternative facts,” they stated. “It’s a fiery post-punk alert from the fringes, illustrating the strength of art and music as tools of resistance.” Olson put the same point more bluntly. “The privileged are few. We have them surrounded. Don’t let them escape. Hold them accountable,” he commented. The video was filmed outside The Woolshed, the band’s rehearsal space at the Waiheke Dirt Track, and shows the four of them playing at night among fire, smoke and Molotov cocktails while cars pass on the road behind them. The track itself runs 3:16, built on rolling drums, distorted guitar and a chanted refrain that treats authoritarian politics as a fairground barker’s routine. Because You’ve Been Good by Trauma Party About Trauma Party Trauma Party are a four-piece from Waiheke Island in New Zealand, playing post-punk with garage-rock and psychedelic elements. The line-up is Buddy Olson on vocals, Derek Solomon on guitar and backing vocals, Ron K on bass and Kirsty Swanney on drums. The band built their first set of songs over roughly fifteen months of live shows before recording them, working out of the Dirt Track rehearsal space they call The Woolshed. That material became “Because You’ve Been Good”, their debut EP, released on 17 April 2026 with four tracks: “Are We in Heaven”, “Speak To Me”, “Sharks” and “Roll Up (It’s The New Truth)”. The band describe the record as drawn from highlights of the live show. Recording took place at the Dirt Track and at Vanguard Studios, where Derek Solomon also mixed. Mastering went to Martin Bowes at The Cage in Coventry, the studio Bowes has run alongside his own long-running project Attrition, whose most recent studio album “The Black Maria” arrived in 2024. Bek Farr designed the sleeve. The EP has been issued independently through the band’s own Bandcamp page, where it is available digitally. “Roll Up (It’s The New Truth)” completes the run of videos taken from it. No follow-up release or tour dates have been announced.
items._cn_summary: 这首单曲以滚动鼓击、失真吉他与吟唱式副歌构成，把威权政治的语言比作嘉年华吆喝。乐队在排练场外夜间拍摄视频，现场有火焰、烟雾和燃烧瓶，汽车从身后驶过，以视觉强化对抗姿态。歌曲的创作背景指向政治语言失去原意、“新真相”与另类事实的荒诞，乐队称其是来自边缘的后朋克警报，强调艺术和音乐作为抵抗工具。该作品出自四人乐队的首张唱片，唱片在排练空间和录音室录制，吉他手完成混音，母带由英国音乐人马丁·鲍斯处理。乐队在演出中积累素材，风格带有车库摇滚和迷幻元素。

items.body: Fear often does its most elaborate work while the body sleeps. Dreams build disasters without waiting for evidence: rooms close around us, familiar faces become unreadable, and futures that never occur leave the nervous system convinced it has survived them. The mind may be rehearsing danger in the name of protection, yet the rehearsal can feel as real as the threat. By morning, a person may carry the emotional debris of an event that existed only behind closed eyes. Copenhagen-based producer, composer, and multi-instrumentalist Trentemøller unveils his latest single, Terrified, drifting into that delicate zone of tension between fear and dreaming. The track, a collaboration with Mew’s Jonas Bjerre, marks the introduction to Trentemøller’s self-titled eighth studio album, set for release on November 13 via his In My Room imprint. Bjerre penned the lyrics, provides the vocals, and directed the accompanying visuals. Terrified places anxiety inside a surprisingly radiant frame. A firm beat holds together dreampop guitars and clear synths that carry the spacious, melodic lift of late-1980s alternative music, while Bjerre’s high, daydreaming voice travels above the arrangement with an almost weightless composure. The song’s brightness lends fear an uncanny buoyancy, allowing dread and wonder to occupy the same three minutes. “When the instrumental was done, I sent it to Jonas Bjerre with a few melody ideas, which he took further while adding new melodies of his own,” Trentemøller says. Bjerre approached the words as an account of the mind preparing itself for dangers that may never leave the realm of sleep. “I think sometimes when you dream about things that make you fearful and uneasy, it’s your mind trying to prepare you for any scenario, like you’re processing catastrophes that have not and may not ever happen.” Traces of the song’s shoegaze beginnings remain in the guitar bloom, although Trentemøller deliberately brought its hooks and electronic details into harder focus. “‘Terrified’ is probably the poppiest song on the album. In its original form it sounded a lot more shoegazey, but I wanted it to be crisper and clearer, less washed out. So I went for synths that almost sound like human voices, with a magical, otherworldly quality to them.” Bjerre’s video extends that tension through animated collage, live-action footage, photography, and hand-built compositing. Apartment blocks and leafless woods become an acid-red interior world inhabited by cut-out figures, animal forms, classical busts, staring eyes, and yellow flowers. White flecks gather into snow or stars; faces pass through paint and layered exposures; a corridor seems to wait at the far end of sleep. Its rough paper edges and saturated color preserve the touch of the hand, turning the city into a roaming succession of fears, recollections, and brief flashes of beauty. Watch the video for Terrfied below: Across ten tracks, trentemøller follows 2024’s Dreamweaver by pushing the meeting point between electronic production and guitar music toward greater extremes, moving among noise-heavy rock, dream pop, shoegaze, darkwave, and direct pop melody. For the first time on a Trentemøller album, every song includes vocals. Alongside Bjerre, he folds those voices into the instrumentation across a cast that includes Sakura, German-British musician Anika, Sune Rose Wagner of The Raveonettes, Midwife’s Madeline Johnston, New Mexico duo Tan Cologne, and Danish singer-songwriter Emma Acs, now a member of Trentemøller’s live band. Trentemøller wrote, performed, produced, and mixed the record, while the singers contributed remotely, often recording their parts at home. The method joins solitary construction to an unusually broad range of voices, bringing the contrast that has defined his work since The Last Resort into a more explicitly song-led form. trentemøller arrives November 13 via In My Room on digital formats, red vinyl, CD, and cassette. Pre-order the album here. trentemøller by trentemøller Trentemøller will bring the album to Europe in February and March 2027, with plans for his band to perform the record from beginning to end. items._cn_summary: Trentemøller与Mew主唱Jonas Bjerre合作推出新单曲“Terrified”，收入其同名第八张专辑。歌曲将恐惧感置于明亮的音乐框架中，坚实的节拍支撑起dreampop吉他与清澈合成器，Bjerre的高音轻盈地漂浮于编曲之上，使焦虑与梦幻共存。歌词源于Bjerre对梦境的观察：大脑在睡眠中演练可能永远不会发生的灾难，以此准备面对未知。Trentemøller表示该曲是专辑中最具流行感的一首，原本更接近shoegaze，后来他刻意让声音更清晰、少些模糊，并选用了近似人声的合成器，营造超现实气质。Bjerre执导的视觉作品结合动画拼贴、实拍影像与手工合成，呈现公寓、树林、剪影人物与眼睛等意象，强化了梦境与恐惧交织的氛围。专辑共十首歌，延续了2024年《Dreamweaver》的方向，探索梦境、记忆与情感之间的微妙地带。

items.body: Texas electro-industrial veterans Mentallo & The Fixer are returning to one of the defining records in their catalog with a newly remastered edition of Where Angels Fear To Tread, due digitally October 16 through Re:Mission Entertainment, followed by its first-ever vinyl pressing on November 20. Originally released by Zoth Ommog in Europe in 1994 and licensed by Metropolis Records for North America the following year, Where Angels Fear To Tread was the third full-length from brothers Gary and Dwayne Dassing, following No Rest For The Wicked and Revelations 23. Its 13-track original sequence includes enduring club staples Decomposed, Sacrilege, and Atom Smasher, songs that helped cement the duo’s place in the harsher, more rhythmically adventurous wing of 1990s electro-industrial music. Alfa Matrix later revisited the album as part of its 2014 Zothera CD box set, though that edition featured new artwork. For the 2026 edition, Jeff Mortimer at JM Mastering has prepared a fresh remaster for vinyl and digital, while Nathan Winter of Industriarts restored the original artwork. The physical edition expands the album to 15 tracks with two remixes and arrives as a 2LP gatefold pressed on yellow and red inverted splatter vinyl, limited to 250 copies worldwide. The gatefold also includes complete lyrics and new commentary from Gary Dassing on the making of the record. The album came together through a home-recording process that now feels almost archaeological in its limitations, with the brothers working from cassette masters while sequencing their synthesizers by computer and stretching a modest setup as far as it could go. “All master recordings at this time were recorded straight to cassette, believe it or not,” says Gary Dassing. “No multi track recording was involved. All vocals were recorded live as the computer sequencer would run the synthesizers. Crazy to think about it, the art of home recording and how far technology has come. ‘Look ma, no equipment necessary! Just some software and a laptop!’ Dwayne and I were sort of flying blind at the time. Everything was a learning experience, and a costly one. New tech in those years was extremely expensive, so you had to be dedicated. Hell, I remember when Dwayne and I lived off bean and cheese tacos just to get that next piece of gear. We were addicted.” The digital edition goes deeper into the archive with seven remixes and 20 tracks in total. It is available to pre-order now through Bandcamp ahead of its October 16 release across streaming platforms, while the vinyl edition is expected to ship November 20. The reissue continues Re Entertainment’s ongoing work with the Mentallo & The Fixer catalogue, following remastered editions of No Rest For The Wicked, Vengeance Is Mine, and Love Is the Law, alongside renewed attention to related projects Reign of Roses and Kitty Kosmonaut. You can order the vinyl version of Where Angels Fear To Tread here. items._cn_summary: 该专辑是德州工业电子组合Mentallo & The Fixer于1994年发行的第三张全长作品，此次以全新重制版形式首次推出黑胶唱片，并追加两首混音曲目。原始录音采用直接录制至卡带的单轨方式，人声与合成器同步实时完成，制作条件极为有限，却塑造出粗粝而富有冲击力的声响。数字版额外收录七首混音，共二十轨，进一步呈现创作过程的延伸脉络。专辑中的多首曲目曾是俱乐部常客，体现了九十年代电子工业音乐中更具节奏冒险性的一面。重制版由Jeff Mortimer负责母带处理，Nathan Winter修复原版封面，内页附完整歌词及Gary Dassing对制作历程的回顾，适合关注工业电子历史脉络与低保真制作手法的听众。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组GuldGanger的数字化EP首作，由经验丰富的民谣歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔，五首作品以传统曲目为主，仅一首由成员Morten Musicus原创。音乐整体弥漫着古老而粗粝的气息，开场曲《Svennedal》以起伏的节奏和富有说服力的人声展现乐队面貌；《Nordgård》中口弦和风笛带来持续推动力；钦巴龙琴为《Agnete Af Bjergmanden》铺设细腻背景；终曲《Ormsö》以弹性口弦与长笛、弦乐交织，营造出奇崛而令人兴奋的器乐效果。这张EP虽短，却显示出乐队成熟而完整的驾驭能力，是对北欧传统音乐的一种个性化、略带实验触感的呈现。

items.body: From dub to industrial and Tanzania to Thailand, from an untitled album by an unnamed artist to a turntable album without records, our Electronic Music Preview has it all! This adventurous slate is bound to appeal to the mind as well as to the body. Site favorites such as Jónsi and Andy Bell appear in surprising categories, while newcomers make their play for the big time. One thing is sure: the dance floors won’t be empty this season. We’re halfway through our Fall Music Preview, with much more to come; our largest installment is set to appear tomorrow! Our cover image comes from Petrels’ Infangthief, covered below. Bonobo is the biggest name on fall’s electronic slate. Fans won’t have long to wait, as Distance in Static is released on September 11. As with previous efforts, the album offers a mix of vocal and instrumental cuts, the bonus being that the vocal tracks are in English, Urdu and Japanese. We’re enamored with lead cut “Drift,” and expect mainstream success (Ninja Tune). The same (safe) prophecy holds true for Chrome Sparks‘s Ball of Light, especially as the producer has roped in Khalid and Jónsi for lead single Sleeper. The languid opener is not representative of the album as a whole; for a more accurate representation, spin the club-friendly title track and then “Pleasure” (Chrome Sounds/AWAL, September 11). Nathan Fake is back, and it didn’t even take that long! The Caldera EP is a follow-up to Evaporator and the Hypercube EP from February and May (InFiné, October 23).   Bibio & Dorian Concept are releasing the expressive Answers, their first collaborate album after years of friendship. The timbres are warm and inviting, perfect for autumn (Warp, October 16). It’s only fair that we mention The Avalanches, though we’re not yet sure if the album is primarily vocal or instrumental; the sample-based Since I Met You is still one of our all-time favorite albums, and we’d love the same to be true for No Bad Memories, out October 16 and preceded by Can’t Get Over Losing You. Another sample-based artist, Odd Nosdam, is releasing a “love letter to the vinyl format.” On Patrol is packed with slow beats, obscure loops, and enthralling grooves: a crate digger’s delight. Bonus points for the cool cover art, seen right (Alien Transistor, October 23).   Is it acid? Is it jazz? Is it ambience? Is it hardcore? Yes ~ Semiratruth‘s S!M is all of these things and more, hopping genres like low fences in a wide field. A lot of ground is covered in twenty-two tracks, not one longer than 3:04 (Sooper, September 25). Space Afrika‘s Quiet Storm is a study in contrasts: featuring segments of ambience, electronics, opera, hip-hop and modern composition. The support cast is massive, each guest contributing a different aspect of a greater story. A spiritual thread runs through the recording, lifting it to a higher level (Dais, September 25). The snails seen on Carmen Villain‘s Memoira are purposeful; the album is one of “deceleration,” with trumpet, clarinet, flute, piano and strings, all filtered through sluggish beats and dub timbres (Smalltown Supersound, September 4). Post Dub Cities is the new concept album from Adriano Zanni, who wanders an unpopulated landscape and finds it rich in sound. The accompanying photos makes it seem less science fiction than recent history (Bronson Recordings, October 2). Soaked in crackle and reverb, Oblique‘s Ghost Dubs is an exercise in tension and mood. Opening single “Low Times” comes with a series of alternate mixes (Pressure, September 25).   Alien Alarms are Tuned to Different Frequencies. The album investigates a wealth of tonalities, uses creative composition to address the modern malaise of distraction. “The machine is much, but it is not everything” (PATCHWORKS, October 2). พังและแพง splits the difference between ambient and electronic on หัดขับรถ, whose title means “Learning to Drive.” The Thai producer calls the sound “dance music for introverts” (September 4). James Gorczyca also straddles the line between genres, adding a bit of modern composition on Weights of this world., whose aural presence is accompanied by a “visual world” (September 2). Les Brown‘s The One After That is the concluding part of a loose trilogy. Punchy rhythms accompany kind patterns, with a slightly cinematic lean (September 22). According to Short Span, it was “important to have Eden Aurelius‘s Entre Nous out for summer.” Close enough, as the album shimmers like the low angle of the ever-sinking sun. The further south one lives, the greater the impact will be (September 17). Supporting our theory that 2026 is The Year of Blue, Emily A. Sprague offers Cyano, drenched in blue synth and voice. There are various ways to procure the bonus tracks, including 7″ and Japanese CD; a limited edition RISO booklet is also available (RVNG Intl., October 2). Belbury Poly returns with his ninth album, Sorcery, a set of nostalgic sci-fi synth, referencing the golden 80s of sight and sound (September 25). Those who miss disco will be enamored with Narcoba‘s Pechersk. The title track could be mistaken for an instrumental by the Pet Shop Boys (Nisantashi, October 2). Loula Yorke seems always to be in a positive mood, and the upbeat nature of her personality shines through her music. Starling Sessons is filled to the gills with synth and exudes a playful tone (Truxalis, September 4).   Here’s something we didn’t expect: Infangthief and Outfangthief, a pair of interlocking albums from old fave Petrels. The drone remains intact, while the beats come hard and fast, reflecting the time spent revisiting and remixing. (Denovali, October 16). Church meets club on Music for Air, as the duo of Gamut Inc uses computer-controlled pipe organ to produce sounds more suited to Saturday night than to Sunday morning. We hold out hope that this music might find its way into a forward-thinking worship service (Karlrecords, October 16). Ride bassist Andy Bell joins harp and synthesizer duo Masal for Common Primitives, a lovely album whose rock tones set it apart from others in this article. The moods shift from placid to encouraging, often within single pieces, as new aspects of the music are turned toward the light (Sonic Cathedral, October 9). Names On Tapes offers Ayin, which celebrates the Jewish concept of “absence as potential,” the seat of creation. Clarinet, guitar and electronics emerge from the void (September 4). Then from nothing we travel to NOWHERE, found “between movement and stillness,” as PHILMS explores the liminal spaces like “That Uninspiring Beige Building” (November 17).   Slow and steady wins the race. Never rising above 121 BPMs, Philipp de Castro‘s Morferna is a lesson in restraint. “Oximoro” even includes a sound like that of a tea kettle, waiting to boil (Fala Nocturna, September 18). Peter Gall‘s Drum Seeds allows the percussion to take center stage, enhanced by synth and keys, producing a sound somewhere between jazz and electronic, with a trance-like veneer (Compost, September 4). Vintage drum machines, live drumming from Valentina Magaletti and sporadic punk-energy vocals make Holy Tongue‘s Basilikum an exciting experience. Lead single “Coca” might fit into an adventurous goth set (AD 93, October 4). One might expect to find Future Sounds of Jazz, Volume 16 in another department, but while the series honors jazz, it falls firmly into the electronic category and features exclusive tracks (Compost, September 18).   opo collects seven years of experiments on 666ridims (2020-2026), using unconventional rhythms, infusing the music with a pan-cultural flavor (Meakusma, September 3). Don’t be fooled by the opening track; Max Kutner‘s The Illustrated Interior veers from rock to glitch to percolation to prog. Infused with a sci-fi sheen, the album sounds as literary as its title (September 16). Sporting a wild cover by Kat Williams Illustrations (shown left), Ørdop Wolkenscheidt‘s concept album Stallmeister Rittich vs. the Machine takes as its starting point the 18th century lost and found poem “The Ballad of Stallmeister Rittich,” and builds a narrative around the hero’s journey: music unfolding like a narrative in verse (October 9). The slightly scary House with a Curse arrives with a silent film video and a sense of fun, the Halloween love child of Andrew Waslylk and Tommy Perman. There’s a haunted story in these grooves, perfect for the midnight hour (Clay Pipe Music, October 16). We’re digging the video for “Plastic Minds / Elastic Machines,” from Jeremiah Chiu‘s Edge Conditions; the frames flash with the percussion, and the presentation is a breath of fresh air (International Anthem, October 9). With “eight prepared turntables, four mixers, no records, six hands,” Institut für Feinmotorik is an outlier. Öd (meaning “barren” or “boring”) is anything but; these are the sounds our turntables hide from us, brought out of the shadows and into the light (Faitiche, October 9). J. Juva‘s loop-based Unclocked uses techniques invented by Steve Reich to set patterns against each other in a miasma of sound. Don’t expect an ambient record; the album is packed with beats and patterns, angular at times yet still suited for adventurous club floors (September 25). Slaylor Moon makes angular, unconventional machine music, “pushing keys, buttons, pads, or wheels.” Crisis Make Up! heads in unexpected directions, but is never random (Maple Death, October 9).   The post-industrial sound of DIKDӔDØR has evolved over time, and now includes drum machines and a power mixer. Their sound continues to be bleak and uncompromising, but now ~ perhaps ironically ~ one can dance to it. The Entertainer is released September 9 on Edelfaul. Also in this vein, A Tomb Full of Stars walks a post-apocalyptic landscape, decorating it with echoed words and the sounds of forgotten melodies, rescued from the ash. 1:When the Reflection Passes is released on Varia September 22. Fresh from Birdsong (made with birds only), Megafauna returns with an immersive, industrial, self-titled album. Voidscan appears on one track, lending the project to an even darker hue (Syrup Moose, September 25). While the music is informed by tragedy, Anthony Baldino‘s CONVEYER bleeds dramatic tension, offering not healing but catharsis, scoring the pain beat by devastating beat (BL_K Noise, September 18). After 17 years, Lauren Bousfield (Nero’s Day at Disneyland) returns to claim her throne. After influencing many splattercore sci-fi IDM artists, she hasn’t lost a step. The Grand Reopening EP drops October 16, preceded by the Mormon-sampling single ØBabylon. Beautifully harsh sounds decorate Cenizas 1era Parte, a broken beats and bass set from Lima’s XR1S, with an industrial sheen (nodo, September 10).   The fact that deep glens opened for Autechre last year opens a window into the artist’s sound. carver is intricate and melodic, while defying expectations of where the beats might land next (September 17). The beats are generous on Roel Funcken‘s Kine 3, spanning the length of a double CD. In an unusual confluence, the artist will be opening for Autechre this year. As the title implies, this is the continuation of a series that gets better with each installment (EC Underground, September 4). Machine Records is the perfect landing place for Foel, whose IDM rhythms are mysterious and dark, a reflection of difficult experiences. Gwasagaru means “scatter-disperse,” which is exactly what these beats do while dancing around a melodic core (September 4).   The clever unknown-untitled offers the double 12″ uu05 on September 18, with information revealed a week later. This way, the house-techno rhythms can be appreciated on their own, with wild speculation as to their origins. While the spelling is different from the epic poem and film, “odissiy,” the closing track on maxolydian‘s altre galassie, is meant to score the end of a journey: one that spans the galaxies and ends up safe at home (September 1). Uplift (Butterfly) is the first taste of Tom VR‘s Don’t Know How Fast I’m Moving Until I Hit Something, an upbeat set inspired by the story of koi ascending waterfalls to become dragons (Heart Somersault, September 9). Never far from our consciousness is Subsist & Faith Disciplines, who already has a trio of releases lined up for fall. First out of the gate is Not Charlie‘s Inconformista, a seemingly oxymoronic “reflective dance floor album” that somehow accomplishes the feat (September 4). Fleet offers Percussions from Space, although one should not be able to hear said percussion while in space (September 25). Sci-fi dance floors will be enamored by Cathopsis‘ Solythode, a voyage into the outer limits of the universe (Component, September 4). JØHRN offers frigid techno on Miles of Silence Between Us, using music as a metaphor for relationships (October 16). Steady, pulsing techno dominates Oscar Mulero‘s Between Two Worlds, the 199th release from Semantica paving the way for a landmark celebration (September 25). The consistently surprising Nyege Nyege Tapes returns with Jay Mitta‘s rapid-fire Kazi Kwanza, which showcases the vivid sound of the Tanzanian underground. Get ready to sweat it out, as the BPMs approach 200 on multiple occasions (September 4). The BPMs of Silvan Strauss may not be quite as fast, but they are still hyperactive; SPRINTING also boasts an international cast, primed to bring the producer’s vision to full fruition (Kabul Fire, September 4). We are really looking forward to fabric presents Max Cooper. The tracklisting blends old favorites with exclusives, along with some surprising entries. Ólafur Arnalds, Future Sound of London, Lusine and a Roly Porter remix of a Cooper track all share space in this upbeat mix (fabric, October 2). Richard Allen

items.body: Review by progtime1234567 — It was only recently when I discovered that I really like this band. Even though I've been a fan ofprogressive rock/metal since around 2018, I only ever listened to Pawn Hearts by this band. WhilePawn Hearts is obviously a great album, I think I'm a bigger fan of this album. Van der Graaf Generator is one of those darker-ish sounding prog bands, sort of in the same vein asKing Crimson. For example, the first song "Killer", which is one of the more accessible songs bythis band, deals with themes of loneliness and death. The lyrics describe a shark that kills therest of the fish around it. I take this as a metaphor for someone who pushes everyone away fromthem, despite wanting to have relationships with the people around them. The song's introspectivelyrics are typical for progressive rock, but it is still a far cry from bands like Yes, whose themesusually revolve around literature, but can occasionally deal with darker themes (see the Yes Album). I personally think Van der Graaf Generator is one of the better progressive rock bands from the1970s. Although they never reached the same levels of commercial success like their peers Yes orGenesis, they were very influential on progressive rock and progressive metal. Similarly to KingCrimson, Van der Graaf Generator is your favorite band's favorite band. This album, along with PawnHearts and Godbluff make a solid trilogy of albums.

items._cn_summary: 范德格拉夫发电机乐队的第四张录音室专辑延续了乐队一贯的阴沉色调和内省气质，歌词围绕孤独与死亡等主题展开，以鲨鱼驱赶其他鱼群的意象隐喻主动将他人推开的人际关系困境。音乐风格偏向黑暗前卫，区别于Yes等文学题材为主的乐队，更接近King Crimson的沉重质感。评论者认为该专辑与《Pawn Hearts》《Godbluff》构成了乐队最稳固的三部曲。尽管乐队在商业上不及同时期的Yes和Genesis，但对前卫摇滚和前卫金属领域影响深远，被视为'你最喜欢的乐队最喜欢的乐队'类型的存在。整体而言，这是一张主题深刻、气质阴郁的前卫摇滚作品，适合偏好非主流、带有实验与暗色调的听众。

items.body: For the third episode of our Musical Road to WOMEX, we travel not only in place but also in time: back to Saigon before 1975, when GI bars ran fuzzed-out rock and twist alongside Cải Lương theatres and bolero radio. That’s the era Saigon Soul Revival dug back up in Ho Chi Minh City in 2016, after a handful of musicians found a compilation called Saigon Rock & Soul: Vietnamese Classic Tracks 1968-1974 by Seattle label Sublime Frequencies, and realised nobody was playing that music live anymore. Nhạc kích động, the Western-influenced rock and soul strand of the period, had been banned outright after the war, while gentler nhạc vàng ballads survived. They started as a covers band and ended up writing most of their own catalogue instead. Ten years on, they carry it to WOMEX in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria this October. The band is Nguyễn Anh Minh on vocals, Indy Jeremy Vinh Laville on guitar and đàn nguyệt, Nguyễn Hương Bảo Hiếu on drums, Gabriel Kaouros on bass and percussion, and Đăng Nguyễn Khoa on keys, with traditional player Nguyễn Thị Hải Phượng guesting on đàn tranh and đàn bầu across their records. Their 2019 debut, Họa Âm Xưa, picked up airplay from Iggy Pop’s BBC6 show and France’s Radio FIP. Their second album, Mối Lương Duyên (2024), featured the single “Đám Cưới Nhà Em”, which went on to soundtrack a scene in HBO’s The Sympathizer. That December, the band recorded a live session for KEXP at l’Antipode in Rennes during TransMusicales. Their third album, Chốn Ta Về, releases 11 September via Saigon Supersound, folding in the T’rung bamboo xylophone and the sáo trúc flute alongside guest spots from multi-instrumentalist Đinh Nhật Minh and saxophonist Trần Mạnh Tuấn. From their WOMEX showcase, the band heads straight into a UK and Europe run: Musicport Festival in Whitby on 24 October, London’s Jazz Cafe the next night, then Bristol and Manchester, before continuing through mainland Europe to a Berlin date on 6 November. Below, the band talks about what it means to bring back music that was banned once already, and what they hope it means to a generation of young Vietnamese listeners discovering it for the first time. They also curate a playlist of the tracks that shaped their sound, exclusively for Rhythm Passport. For someone who’s never heard Nhạc Vàng, how would you describe what the band does, and what that sound felt like in the city it came from? Imagine being a teenager in Saigon, Vietnam in the late 1960s. Your grandparents are at a Cải Lương theater watching a traditional form of folk opera, your parents are singing along to a heartfelt nhạc vàng record in a typical Vietnamese bolero style, your auntie is going to a ballroom to dance the cha-cha-cha and on your way to the night market you pass by an American GI bar where a Vietnamese band is playing fuzzed out rock and twist songs for a young lively audience. All this while there is a war raging in the country with no end in sight. As a band we try to capture the essence of this period and imagine what it may have been like if the music of that time continued to develop without interruption until the present day. This music was effectively erased after 1975, when Western pop was banned and replaced. What drew the five of you to dig it back up rather than write something new, and how did you first find your way into these songs? Many classic nhạc vàng songs survived after 1975 and are popular to this day in Vietnam, but the more western influenced dance music, nhạc kích động, which were commonly in the styles of rock, surf, twist and soul were strictly banned and therefore were mostly unknown. When some of the members of SSR came across the compilation “Saigon Rock & Soul: Vietnamese Classic Tracks 1968-1974” we were blown away by the heavy raw sound and were amazed that these old songs were not being performed live to our knowledge, at least not the old versions. This inspired us to look more into such old recordings and start a tribute band to bring that energy back to the stage. You put rock musicians alongside players of the đàn nguyệt and đàn bầu, and let bolero sit next to psychedelia. What makes your version of this revival different from simply covering the originals? Though we started as a tribute band playing cover versions of these old 1960s/70s recordings and trying to really achieve that vintage sound, we eventually started making our own interpretations and ended up writing our own music entirely. In fact most of the songs on our albums are original compositions, many of which incorporate traditional Vietnamese instrumentation and fuse different styles in a very contemporary fashion. We always try to be true to our original inspiration and there are some old songs that are too good not to play, however our live shows and releases mainly consist of original material which we are happy to say has been received very positively. WOMEX is a room full of people who book, release and champion music from everywhere. Who or what are you hoping to connect with while you’re there? For us it’s an amazing opportunity to be able to perform at WOMEX and since Vietnam is not a country that is very present in the international music industry, we feel very privileged to be a part of such a globally recognised event. We do not have a specific agenda but we hope that we can make some good connections that will allow us to share our music and Vietnamese culture further across the world! You’ve built the band on raw, live shows: you’ve described the sound as descending out of the southern night sky. How does playing to a room of industry delegates, rather than a festival crowd, change the way you play? It’s hard to say because this will be our first time performing for a room of industry delegates haha. However, we have played several function gigs for embassies/consulates, hotels etc. and we always manage to connect with our audience and have them dancing by the end of the show. Your music resurrects a specific place and moment: the Saigon of the 1960s and 70s, dense and humid and electric. What’s it like to carry that sound to somewhere as far from it as a small Atlantic island, and does where you play change how it lands? Every place we play at has its own culture and vibe so it’s a pleasure for us to see how people react across the world. We are humans after all so we flow with and adapt to the energy at every show. That being said, we believe that wherever we play, it is our duty to create an atmosphere where people feel immersed in the music and energy we bring. Bringing back suppressed music is an act of memory as much as performance. What do you hope younger Vietnamese listeners, and audiences abroad who don’t know this history, take from it? We live in a very modern technological age where young people are increasingly valuing superficial entertainment and material wealth more than real culture. We hope to encourage the youth around the world to see the value in live performances and we especially wish to inspire our younger Vietnamese listeners to feel proud of their heritage, to appreciate and seek the roots of their culture. That is truly something worth valuing. Your new album Chốn Ta Về means “the place we return to.” What’s the homecoming in it, and where does the band go afterwards: more originals, more digging into the golden era, touring? Chốn Ta Về does not only refer to a literal home or country. The songs on the album tell different stories including ones of love, loss, resilience and acceptance. It’s not so much a matter of identity but a reference to finding our internal peace and our place in this world, no matter what the circumstances. If you could write a personal invitation to the people of Las Palmas to come and discover your showcase, what would it say? ¡Ahul a toda la gente linda de las Islas Canarias! It’s not everyday you get to hear a Vietnamese band that fuses traditional ethnic sounds with heavy contemporary grooves and psychedilia. We will take you on a journey like no other. ¡Dale! Let’s get loose and show us how you party in Las Palmas!   Saigon Soul Revival carry the fuzzed-out rock and soul of wartime Saigon into WOMEX 2026 in Las Palmas on 21 October   PLAYLIST: SAIGON SOUL REVIVAL X RHYTHM PASSPORT   You can find all the previous episodes of Musical Road to Womex HERE The post Musical Road to WOMEX 2026 – Saigon Soul Revival appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
